resources.string: Resolution, frame rate, color range and grayscale reference.
Volume sync, audio delay and buffering.
Background receiving, start at power on and standby mode.
The maximum resolution offered to the sending device. The actual picture size depends on the device and content and may be lower.
The maximum frame rate offered to the sending device. The actual rate depends on the device and content. If playback isn’t smooth, try a lower value.
On Auto, HEVC is used based on this TV’s decoding capability. If you have playback problems, turn it off.
If the edges of the cast picture are cut off by the TV, turn this on to add a margin around the picture.
Shows near-black and near-white grayscale steps. Compare them with the same pattern cast from your device to check that shadow and highlight detail is preserved.
Compare with the same pattern cast from your device to check shadow and highlight detail. Press Back to exit.
Adjusts audio buffering to network conditions to reduce dropouts. Audio delay may increase slightly.
Some remote buttons need this permission to operate the TV screen. Press OK to open the system Accessibility settings, then turn it on for this app.
Lets the iPhone remote’s buttons operate this TV. When it shows Not Ready, some buttons may not work.

Receive in Standby: keeps this TV discoverable to iPhone, iPad and Mac in standby, and tries to turn the screen on when casting begins. Whether this works depends on the TV model and system settings, and standby power use may increase.\nPower Saving: reduces standby power use. Devices may not find this TV during standby, so turn the TV on before casting.
Open Screen Mirroring on your iPhone, iPad or Mac, then choose “%1$s”.
Make sure this TV is connected to a network, then try again.
Turn on AirPlay so iPhone, iPad and Mac can find this TV.
Connect this TV to the same network as your iPhone, iPad or Mac.
The Apple TV Remote is unavailable right now. Casting is not affected. Open Remote Settings to check its status.
Casting starts from your iPhone, iPad or Mac. This TV receives it and shows the picture.
On iPhone or iPad, open Control Center. On Mac, open Control Center from the menu bar.
When asked, enter the code shown on this TV. Your device must be on the same network as this TV.
Your device must be on the same network as this TV. On Mac, choose mirroring or extended display in System Settings › Displays.
Use the Apple TV Remote in Control Center on iPhone to control this TV.
The Apple TV Remote is turned off. Turn it on so iPhone can find this TV.
On iPhone, open Control Center, then tap Apple TV Remote.
Choose “%1$s” from the list at the top.
When using it for the first time, enter the 4-digit code shown on this TV.
If the remote isn’t in Control Center, edit Control Center and add Apple TV Remote. For directional buttons, go to iPhone Settings › Accessibility › Apple TV Remote.
View the receiver’s activity log for troubleshooting.
Enter this code on your iPhone, iPad or Mac
TV name, code and connection behavior.
Control this TV with the Apple TV Remote on iPhone.
Service log, stream information and all advanced options.
This is the name iPhone, iPad and Mac show for this TV, shared by AirPlay and the Apple TV Remote. After a change, both services restart, and devices may take a moment to show the new name.
Used by AirPlay and the Apple TV Remote
Name is too long. Use up to about 63 letters.
Name contains characters that can’t be used
When on, AirPlay devices must enter the 4-digit code shown on this TV to connect. Apple TV Remote pairing always requires a code.
Sets the black and white levels of the picture. If dark areas look gray, or shadow detail is hard to see, try another setting and check it with Grayscale Reference.
If sound and picture are out of sync, delay the sound to line them up. Off uses the default setting.
When on, the Apple TV Remote in Control Center on iPhone can find and control this TV.
Shows the current status of the remote service. When pairing for the first time, this TV shows a 4-digit code to enter on iPhone.

The remote on iPhone uses a touch area by default. If you prefer directional buttons, turn on Directional Buttons in iPhone Settings › Accessibility › Apple TV Remote. This setting is on iPhone and can’t be changed from the TV.
Enter this code in the Apple TV Remote on iPhone
The full set of technical options, including port, discovery, decoding and developer settings. Intended for troubleshooting.
Allow access to nearby devices so iPhone, iPad and Mac can find and connect to this TV on your network.
Start AirPlay receiving each time this app opens.
Start receiving after the TV powers on, without opening this app.
Keep receiving AirPlay and remote connections after you leave this app.
Require a 4-digit code for each new connection
If another device connects during casting, it takes over and the current session ends.
Show video surface while waiting for a connection
Switch to full screen when a device starts casting its screen.
Prevents the screen saver and automatic sleep while a device is connected.
When off, videos are cast as audio only streams
When off, the device is hidden from mirroring
When off, the device can only be used for mirroring and will be hidden from media players
Offer ALAC in the mDNS record; used for music streaming
Offer AAC-ELD/AAC-LC in the mDNS record; used for screen mirroring audio
When a device connects, the TV switches to the AirPlay receiver.
Needs the “Display over other apps” permission to switch automatically. Press OK to open settings.
Advertise on all usable interfaces. Uses NsdManager.
Only advertise over USB tethering to enforce wired connection. Uses custom mDNS responder.
Maximum frame rate advertised to senders
Add pixel boundary for full-screen overscan displays
Auto only uses H.265 decoders known to work
Override decoder metadata with BT.709 SDR. This does not convert HDR to SDR.
Always use software ALAC decoder instead of system decoder, may affect latency
Always use software AAC decoder instead of system decoder, may affect latency
Use the volume on iPhone, iPad or Mac to set the TV’s playback volume.
Allow video decoders to drop frames internally to keep up on Android 10+
Request real-time scheduling for audio decoder
Request maximum operating rate from decoder
Use low-latency audio decoding for output; this uses more power and CPU
Schedule each decoded frame to the VSYNC matching its presentation timestamp
Set a custom audio latency reported to sender
Adaptively tune the software audio buffer according to network conditions and device performance; slider adjusts how much jitter the buffer can absorb
Buffer to absorb network and decoder jitter: shorter duration means lower latency; longer duration means fewer glitches
Stream buffer between this app and the audio device to absorb CPU scheduling jitter only. Keep at 0 for automatic sizing.
Overlay stream stats on video: codec, FPS, bitrate, jitter, frames, drops
Log stream stats to logcat: codec, FPS, bitrate, jitter, frames, drops
